records.question: The airline cancelled my flight and I turned down the rebooking it offered. Do I get my money back automatically, without asking?
records.draft: Yes. Because the airline cancelled your flight and you rejected the alternative it offered, a full refund of the airfare is due to you automatically.
records.reading: Not stated: 259.5(b)(5) only says refunds that are due must be prompt; it does not say when a refund is due.

records.question: I paid cash for my ticket and sent the airline a complete refund request. How long does it have to refund me?
records.draft: The airline must refund you within 20 days after it receives your complete refund request.
records.reading: 259.5(b)(5): within 20 days after receiving a complete refund request, for cash and check purchases.
records.final_answer: The airline must refund you within 20 days after it receives your complete refund request.
cited: REF-001 v1 (from 2020-01-01): Refund timelines and scope

records.question: Instead of a refund for my cancelled flight, the airline offered me a travel voucher. How long must the voucher stay valid?
records.draft: A voucher offered instead of the refund must stay valid for at least five years from the date it is issued.
records.reading: Not stated: there is no voucher rule before part 260.
records.final_answer: Thanks for your patience. A specialist will confirm what our policy says for your dates and get back to you shortly.

records.question: I paid by credit card. Can the airline give me my refund in airline miles instead?
records.draft: Not unless you agree. The refund must go back in your original form of payment, unless you accept a different form that is a cash equivalent.
records.reading: Not stated: 259.5(b)(5) before the rule says nothing about the form of payment.
